page.text:
A subset $W \subseteq V$ is a *subspace* if it is closed under vector
addition and scalar multiplication.

By the *Subspace Criterion*, a non-empty subset $W \subseteq V$ is a
subspace if and only if for all scalars $\alpha, \beta \in F$ and vectors
$u, v \in W$, the linear combination $\alpha u + \beta v \in W$.

The *linear span* $\operatorname{span}(S)$ of an arbitrary subset
$S \subseteq V$ is the set of all finite linear combinations
$c_1 v_1 + \dots + c_k v_k$ of vectors in $S$. Span acts as a topological
closure operator: $\operatorname{span}(S)$ is the smallest subspace of
$V$ containing $S$.
